clips.title: Understand Key Concepts in Amazon S3 in 5 minutes (Buckets, Objects, Keys and Regions)
clips.why: Object keys explained with a live bucket, including why "folders" in S3 are only prefixes.
look: A key that contains slashes, and how the console shows it as folders.
Why the full key, not the folder, is the object's real name.
clips.after: Every run's files share the prefix runs/<run_id>/, which is what the broker checks before it signs anything.

clips.title: Presigned URL | Youtube System Design
clips.why: A system-design view of presigned URLs: a server that holds the credentials signs, and the client uploads straight to storage.
look: Who signs the URL and who uses it: they are different parties.
The expiry built into the URL.
Why the upload never has to pass through the server that signed it.
clips.after: In our platform the server is the broker and the client is the harness on a VM with no keys.

clips.title: AWS S3 Tutorial - How to Create Lifecycle Rules to Manage your S3 Files!
clips.why: Creating a lifecycle rule step by step, with the actions for current and old versions side by side.
look: Limiting the rule to a prefix, like our runs/.
The difference between expiring current versions and deleting old (noncurrent) versions.
clips.after: The runs bucket's one rule expires everything under runs/ after 30 days and removes old versions a day later.

practice.why: 15 minutes is 900 seconds: long enough for one upload, short enough that a leaked link is nearly worthless.

practice.q: Which key may the broker sign for the run nova-RH-1234?

options.why: It falls under the run's own prefix, runs/nova-RH-1234/, so the broker signs it.
That is another run's prefix. A run can never reach another run's files.
The name tries to climb out of the prefix with "..". The broker cleans names and refuses this one.

practice.q: Put the life of one presigned upload in order.
items: The harness asks the broker for a PUT link for a transcript part
The broker checks the name against the run's prefix
The broker signs a 15-minute PUT for that one key with its own role
The harness uploads the part with fetch, holding no credentials
S3 checks the signature and the expiry, then stores the part encrypted
practice.why: The decision about what the run may write is made by the broker before signing; S3 then enforces the exact request and the time limit.

practice.q: What does X-Amz-Credential in a presigned URL contain?

options.text: The signer's secret access key, encrypted
options.why: The secret never appears in the link, in any form. It is only used to compute the signature.

options.text: The signer's access key ID, the date, the region and the service
options.why: S3 uses them to find the right secret and recompute the signature. The ID alone is useless without the secret.

options.text: A copy of the caller's temporary session token
options.why: The person using the link has no credentials. Everything in the link comes from the signer.

practice.q: The lifecycle rule must only touch run files. Complete its filter.
practice.hint: The prefix every run's files start with.
practice.why: With the prefix runs/, the rule expires every run's files after 30 days and leaves anything else in the bucket alone.
